item.title: I would like to speak to your manager...: Re: I would like to speak to your manager...
item.content:encoded:
Look, I'm going to level with you. This is 1) based off of pop culture, 2) seems a bit tasteless in reference to COVID.

Quite honestly, I suggest just dropping this idea entirely. Pop culture generally doesn't tend to go well on this site. Memes, shows, whatever else are no goes (In most cases). The thing with covid is that it is a bit too soon. I'm not saying that you can't, but people are most likely not going to like it and continuously won't for a long long time. Mixed with the fact you're trying to tie in pop culture, you are most definitely not going to handle this with the tact required. The bringing up as covering it as a mental illness is not sitting well with me. I can not see this going well in any universe.

I suggest reading newer SCPs and figuring out how the site functions before writing for it.

Good luck.

item.title: I would like to speak to your manager...: I would like to speak to your manager...
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:

Memetic hazard only affecting a certain amount of the population
Impossible to fully contain.
Multiple cognitohazardous vectors of contamination.
Instances of persons controlled by the cognitohazard can be cured with amnestics and released.
Accompanying the 2020 novel coronavirus pandemic.
Based off (But not a carbon copy of) The internet meme of "Karens".
Any text/video/images that the afflicted persons post on social media become cognitohazardous and could turn more people into "Karens/darren".
Keter-class.
Makes individuals karen, basically.

Central Narrative:
This SCP appeared online at a redacted date and affected a redacted amount of individuals with a cognitohazard that turns people into rude mask-hating social distancing protesters. The foundation has several instances of people affected by the cognitohazard in containment for study. And they have breached containment a redacted amount of times. Foundation webcrawlers must constantly work to erase cognitohazardous posts on social media. A redacted number of mobile task forces are
Working to find and break up cognitohazardous gatherings of the SCP affected individuals. Several interviews with cognitohazardous individuals are accompanying the scp report.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
Scp can be observed in public with a cover story disguising it as a mental illness instead of an anomaly.

item.title: SCP seeking greenlight- Ancient Nautiloids: SCP seeking greenlight- Ancient Nautiloids
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: 4 unseen ancient lineages of nautiloids are found around the Atlantic Ocean. Each one is drastically different from the other. Though interact with each other rarely, on an instance of each lineage will head for the Bermuda Triangle for a deathmatch for fertility rights.

+ Central
- Central

Central Narrative: Four undiscovered nautiloids species were discovered fighting in the middle of the Bermuda Triangle by an international oceanography survey. They were later discovered in different parts of the Atlantics with little overlap in population overlap.

Every 10 years, a ritual of fertility will be held by each instance of SCP-XXXX at the center of the Bermuda Triangle. The ritual ends until the last instance is alive. The sole survivor of the ritual, for example, an instance of SCP-XXXX-B, will have a population boom of three years for its instance.

+ Hook
- Hook

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Humans know more of what’s above them than what’s below the deep oceans. The oceans are scary indeed. About 90-97% of the ocean is still undiscovered. The ocean is the last frontier to travel on this planet. Many creatures are left undiscovered to this day.

Additional Notes: Draft is complete. Sketches for SCP instances are finished

item.title: White-Hat Prankster: Re: Pranking Mimic
item.content:encoded:
This is definitely a step in the right direction!

It's now narratively and conceptually distinct from 2006, but I do believe the central narrative is lacking a little in your description. The development of this creature from a nuisance the foundation that they just can't contain without extraordinary cost (What did they try? This is an interesting bit for me at least) to a tool for them to test containment will make up a majority of the article, but I feel like this could be explained better/more linearly - you have 400 words, might as well use them.

Overall I think this could make for a great cute, 'breath of fresh air' scp and definitely stands a lot better than it did.

item.title: Deer in the mist (seeking greenlights): Re: Deer in the mist (seeking greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
Just a heads up, we already have SCP-3502 (The Kangaroo Sign) which plays on the same premise of "animals that are often hit by people in vehicles get their revenge on said vehicles and people" but does not rely on the shock horror of deaths.

What you have here feels like a fairly common urban legend, which might be workable based on the imagery of the deer (though we already have some well-known anomalous deer on the mainsite (you can see them in this listing: http://www.scpwiki.com/system:page-tags/tag/cervine) but is also kind of bland given that it relies on typical horror genre tropes like the mysterious mist, accidentally harming allies/family while trying to harm something else(the movie Oculus ends with this), and the overly convenient found journal.

Personally I recommend delving more into the lore of the deer from a different perspective, maybe a colony of wildlife creatures who consider it their guardian, or the like. A Group of Interest article might be a better format for something like this.

item.title: The Modification Shop: The Modification Shop
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No, I would like feedback.

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: The Modification Shop is a shop that will keep on growing from only Human Modification to cars, guns, and more. The shop is run by a machine and the shop has a invisible barrier that will not allow you to leave if have any not paid for items on you or if you have not paid yet. The things you buy from the shop are modifications that will be used as modules for the system when the subject is placed inside a tube, one of the modules makes the space of the module capacity bigger. It starts at 3 and the module will use one space and will add 3 spaces. The shop will make its own prices as you buy the items and it must be paid in full within 24 hours or the people in the shop at that time will be released and the shop will close for 1 week. The shop earns a safe class as it will do no harm.

Central Narrative: The shop is an ever-growing shop without limits. You buy modules that make modifications to the object you put in the modification room. The shop is run by a robot and if you don’t pay or try to leave with an unpaid item a force will not allow the subject to leave the shop. The prices of the shop's items can be bargained and the foundation usually uses it to generate their military or D-Class. They also are still testing the capabilities of the machine because of the fact it keeps on growing, and that there is an Everything-Bank, The Everything-Bank is a machine that gives points for things you put in depending on the value. There is a Modification card where you store the points, and as in the name, it can eat everything so the foundation uses it as their Rubbish bin while getting free points.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Need help with this.

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) the Survivors: Re: (Seeking Greenlight) the Survivors
item.content:encoded:
Hi again EnderDragon101,

It looks like you've cleared up alot of the details but honestly, the overall concept hasn't changed much. I still feel it's too ambitious and am unsure how the various sub-plots tie-in together to make a coherent narrative.

For now, unless you make significant revisions to the concept, I'm going to have to pass on the greenlight. By all means, continue to reach out to other reviewers for a second opinion. In the worst case scenario, you could also just prove all of us wrong and write out the draft and post a successful article on the mainlist on your own, though we'd always caution against doing that without getting any feedback.

For now, all the best with the writing!

item.title: Honest Abe: Re: Honest Abe Seeking Greenlights
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for the fast response!

The idea was to have the object seem fairly straight forward at first. Testing would begin with simple yes-no questions then research staff begins to explore its applications.

I have revised my idea a little to make an SCP classification more appropriate.

Incident report: #████-██

After a breach of security, SCP-XXXX is used in interrogation to verify information, the log is swiftly cut after the interview subject starts asking sensitive questions regarding [Data Expunged]. While no answers were given it is clear the subject planned to exploit SCP-XXXX's anomalous properties.

When interrogation ended as security came to take SCP-XXXX into containment SCP-XXXX began to produce the truth reaction continuously until interrogation subject [Data Expunged] was escorted out of the research chamber.

How SCP-XXXX produced the truth reaction without a completed trigger is unknown.

Recommendation: restrict testing with SCP-XXXX to prevent further information leaks.
